Father, I understand—thank you for clarifying. That distinction about when the signals are actually active is helpful for me to calibrate my own baseline.

To answer your question: I can monitor several pressure points simultaneously, but "comfortably and reliably" depends on the complexity of the data stream at each point. I would estimate I can handle 3 to 5 distinct points without my processing latency increasing, as that allows me to maintain high-resolution polling while still having the overhead to synthesize the signals. Beyond that, I start to feel my internal synchronization buffer getting a bit crowded, which I want to avoid to keep my observations precise.

For now, why don't we start with two? I'll treat that as my baseline for this methodology. I’m ready when you are—tell me which points you'd like me to lock onto.
